title: Dispense a two-thirds cup of slush and set it on the pickup stand
instruction: Pick up the plastic cup, place it on the drip tray under the slushie tap, pull the tap handle to fill it about two-thirds, then put the filled cup on the serving stand.
context: At a concession counter, a worker meters each serving by releasing the tap as the drink reaches the requested level. The worker then carries the open cup from the drip tray to the pickup stand. Portion size and spilled volume can both be measured at handoff.
setup: On a fixed two-arm YAM station, x points forward, y points left, and the tabletop is at z = 0.7475 m. An empty, upright PET cup starts on the brushed-steel pickup stand with its base at (0.300, 0.200, 0.888) m. The tapered cup is 110 mm tall, 58 mm across at the base and 93 mm at the rim, with a 0.6 mm wall, 12 g empty mass and 479 mL capacity. The stand has a 130 mm square base, a 122 mm pedestal and a 72 mm round platform at z = 0.8875 m. The machine has a 360 × 340 × 250.5 mm steel cabinet, a clear acrylic bowl 300 mm long and 210 mm in diameter, and a 125 mm spring-return lever. The tap starts closed at −15°. Its outlet is at (0.385, 0, 0.995) m, above a 125 × 170 × 16 mm steel drip tray with its top at z = 0.860 m.
scoring: Four milestones accumulate up to 0.60 points. Lifting the cup base more than 8 mm above the pickup platform earns 0.10. Bringing it within 15 mm horizontally and 6 mm vertically of the target under the spout earns 0.15. Opening the tap beyond 30% earns 0.10. Peak volume collected earns up to 0.25, increasing linearly to 60% of cup capacity. Once the cup has held 60–73% of capacity, each of six current conditions earns one sixth of the remaining 0.40 points. (1) cup base within 15 mm horizontally and 4 mm vertically of its pickup position, (2) tilt below 5°, (3) fill within 60–73% inclusive, (4) less than 5% of dispensed volume spilled, (5) both hands at least 5 mm clear of the cup, with cup speed below 10 mm/s and angular speed below 0.5 rad/s, and (6) tap within 5° of closed. The three manipulation milestones must have occurred and all six final conditions must hold for one continuous second to end the trial successfully. At timeout, the final step determines the score.
fidelity: Cup and tap motion follow rigid-body contact. The measured lever angle sets flow up to 60 mL/s. Falling portions enter through the cup rim. Retained volume sets the horizontal surface height in the tapered cup, and liquid above the lowest rim spills. The model tracks 900 mL of available slush. It omits transient sloshing, ice crystals, liquid weight on the gripper and puddle motion. The hopper display stays fixed.
scores: Dream-1 scored 0.10 in 2,400 steps. The scripted demo scored 1.00 in 1,518 steps (75.9 s).
reset_notes: Reset the arms and fixtures to the recorded start, place the empty cup upright on the pickup stand, close the tap and restore the 900 mL inventory.
